ONE-TO-ONE COACHING WITH JOSH BARBEE

Real conversations.
Change you can practice.

A focused space to understand your patterns, work through what matters, and choose how you want to show up.

BRING WHAT’S REAL

Start with the part
that feels stuck.

You don’t need a polished explanation. Bring the conversation you keep avoiding, the argument that keeps repeating, or the connection you want to build.

  • Communicating without shutting down or escalating
  • Setting boundaries with clarity and care
  • Building confidence in dating and partnership
  • Taking responsibility and repairing after conflict
  • Being more present in friendship and family life

HOW THE WORK TAKES SHAPE

Clarity. Practice.
Follow-through.

Coaching connects what you discover in conversation with what you do in daily life.

Get clear on what matters.

Explore your situation, what you want to change, and what a healthier relationship would look like to you.

Understand the pattern.

Look at the beliefs, habits, and reactions that influence how you connect. Identify the choices you can make differently.

Try something concrete.

Choose a practical next step: a conversation, a boundary, a listening practice, or a commitment you can follow through on.

Reflect and keep building.

Review what happened, notice what helped, and adjust. Progress comes from practicing, reflecting, and trying again.

A FEW THINGS YOU MAY BE WONDERING

Before you begin.

Do I need to be in a relationship?

No. You can work on how you date, build friendships, connect with family, or prepare for a future relationship. The starting point is how you want to show up.

Will coaching help me change my partner?

The focus is on your own choices: how you communicate, listen, set boundaries, and follow through. Another person’s choices remain their own. Coaching does not promise a particular relationship outcome.

Is coaching the same as therapy?

Coaching focuses on goals, relationship skills, and everyday practice. It does not diagnose or treat mental health conditions and is not a substitute for therapy.

What if talking about feelings doesn’t come naturally?

That’s a valid starting point. You can begin with a specific situation and work toward words that feel honest to you. You don’t need to arrive with a particular vocabulary.

How do I book, and what does it cost?

Booking, session details, and pricing will be shared when scheduling opens. In the meantime, use the short reflection on the Start Here page to clarify what you’d like to work on.
